data.title: Indonesian anger builds over wildfires and toxic haze
data.description: JAKARTA - Indonesians protested in several cities on Tuesday, raging against wildfires and a toxic haze that has made thousands unwell for weeks on end in a crisis that has engulfed Southeast Asia.

data.title: Alberta votes to remain part of Canada
data.description: CALGARY - Alberta residents voted to remain part of Canada in the province’s first-ever referendum on separation, in a much-needed win for Prime Minister Mark Carney as he attempts to unify the country amid a trade war with the United States.

data.title: Unhappy republic: France’s troubles extend beyond the street
data.description: PARIS - “Revolution!” some shouted during France’s protests. Others demanded better classroom conditions. Many simply wanted their household budgets to stop shrinking as fuel and food prices spike.

data.title: UN says 19 million Afghans facing ‘acute food insecurity’
data.description: GENEVA - The number of people facing acute food insecurity in Afghanistan is set to rise above 19 million during the forthcoming winter season, the United Nations warned on Tuesday.

data.title: Zelensky and US envoys seek to repair frayed ties
data.description: OSLO - Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky is preparing to hold talks with top US envoys in Norway on Tuesday in a bid to get strained relations with Washington “on a more constructive path”, Oslo said.

data.title: North Korea releases Kim photos to counter death rumours
data.description: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has appeared in photographs released by state media during a visit to a clothing exhibition, as speculation about his health and rumoured death circulates online.

data.title: Rubio lands in India for ‘trade diplomacy’
data.description: MUMBAI - US Secretary of State Marco Rubio arrived in India on Tuesday, his second official visit to the country this year, as he pursues an Asian tour blending diplomacy and trade.

data.title: Settler violence becomes a liability for Israeli PM
data.description: JERUSALEM - Attacks on a US journalist and European diplomats in the occupied West Bank have turned Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s championing of settlers into a potential liability days before elections, with opponents calling him soft on “Jewish terrorism”.

data.title: France to impose new curfews where necessary: PM
data.description: PARIS — France will impose new curfews in areas where needed on Tuesday, Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu said, adding that the measures introduced in several cities the previous day had "helped keep the night calm".

data.title: Indonesia investigates crash of suspected Chinese rocket fragment
data.description: JAKARTA — Indonesian authorities were investigating on Tuesday after a car-sized piece of what a government agency said was a Chinese space rocket crashed into a palm oil plantation near homes and work sites.

data.title: ‘Online echo chamber’ amplifies political violence threats in Australia
data.description: SYDNEY - Australia’s security chiefs had warned of “online echo chambers” fuelling grievances and conspiracies and stepped up prosecutions for threats of political violence ahead of Monday’s attack on a lawmaker in a rural town.

data.title: South Korea to reduce Ukraine embassy staff after PoW row
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea's foreign ministry said on Tuesday it would withdraw some staff from its embassy in Ukraine, as a diplomatic row deepens over the transfer of North Korean prisoners of war to Seoul.

data.title: Seoul warns of ‘firm’ response to North Korea’s border threats
data.description: SEOUL - South Korea’s military warned Tuesday of a “firm” response and resolute punishment for any further provocations by North Korea, saying it was “unacceptable” for Pyongyang to blame Seoul for escalating tensions.

data.title: Too much of a good scent? Hanoi trims iconic trees
data.description: HANOI - Vietnam's capital Hanoi has launched a large-scale programme to prune hundreds of its iconic blackboard trees and is considering relocating some after their distinctive fragrance proved too much for some residents.

data.title: Curfew imposed in parts of Paris
data.description: PARIS - ⁠French ​authorities imposed a night curfew on the Place de la Republique ​and streets around ‌Les Halles in Paris from ⁠2000 GMT on Monday night (3am Tuesday, Thailand) until 0400 ​GMT on Tuesday, French ​broadcaster BFM ‌reported, ​following riots over the weekend amid nationwide protests.

data.title: Hong Kong police arrest woman after dog thrown into sea
data.description: A woman has been arrested on suspicion of animal cruelty after allegedly throwing a dog into the sea in Hong Kong.

data.title: Hong Kong police arrest woman after dog allegedly thrown into sea
data.description: A woman has been arrested on suspicion of animal cruelty after allegedly throwing a dog into the sea in Hong Kong.

data.title: Australian MP crushed in car attack loses a leg
data.description: WANGARATTA, Australia - Australian lawmaker Helen Haines has lost a leg after being struck by a car in a deliberate attack, local media reported on Tuesday.

data.title: EU unveils strategy to boost Arctic presence
data.description: BRUSSELS (BELGIUM) - The EU is to unveil plans to bolster its foothold in the Arctic Tuesday, as it grapples with pressure from Russia and the United States in the key strategic region.

data.title: Detained Suu Kyi receives UK royal package: Myanmar govt
data.description: YANGON - Myanmar's Aung San Suu Kyi received a package from Britain's King Charles III on Monday, authorities said, releasing the first pictures of the detained Nobel laureate in two months and describing her as a "special female prisoner".

data.title: Ukraine races to secure energy supplies ahead of winter
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Hardly a day goes by now in Ukraine without news of another Russian air strike on the country's energy sector, causing widespread blackouts, including in the capital, Kyiv.

data.title: Israel announces arrests after West Bank settler attacks on Westerners
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israeli police said Monday they had arrested 10 people in the occupied West Bank after settler attacks on an American photographer and a French mayor that drew international condemnation but mixed messages from the government.

data.title: Ukraine on back foot as Kremlin moots US, China meeting
data.description: KYIV (UKRAINE) - Ukraine on Monday again said it had no early warning of powerful Russian missile strikes and complained that persistent problems with a US military grade satellite were hobbling frontline troops.

data.title: Kenyan cult leader guilty on all charges over 191 starvation deaths
data.description: MOMBASA (KENYA) - A self-proclaimed Kenyan preacher and his associates were on Monday found guilty of murdering 191 people, mostly children, in an infamous starvation cult.

data.title: Ethiopia PM warns Eritrea of 'severe consequences' if supports enemies
data.description: ADDIS ABABA - Ethiopia's Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed warned Eritrea on Monday that it faces "severe consequences" if it continues to support rebels in his country.

data.title: Netanyahu basks in Trump endorsement week before election
data.description: JERUSALEM - Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Monday basked in Donald Trump's endorsement days before close-fought elections, airing a call in which the US president predicted he would win and suggested they may again attack Iran together.

data.title: Japan launches rocket for potential world first Mars moon mission
data.description: TOKYO - Japanese scientists launched a spacecraft Tuesday that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars's moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth.

data.title: UN climate panel head wants swift end to deadlock over key scientific report
data.description: GENEVA (SWITZERLAND) - The world's top climate scientists will reconvene at the earliest opportunity, the panel's chair said on Monday, after member states failed to agree when to release its crucial new findings on global heating.

data.title: Putin, Xi and Trump could meet at APEC summit: Kremlin
data.description: MOSCOW - The Russian, Chinese and US presidents, Vladimir Putin, Xi Jinping and Donald Trump, could potentially meet at an upcoming Asia-Pacific summit in China, the Kremlin said on Monday.

data.title: Albanian PM warns of 'red line' after days of unrest
data.description: TIRANA (ALBANIA) - Albanian Prime Minister Edi Rama accused protesters of crossing a "red line" Monday after a police station was set ablaze during anti-government demonstrations.

data.title: Indonesia fires have burned nearly two million hectares: monitor
data.description: JAKARTA (INDONESIA) - Fires in Indonesia that have caused a regional haze crisis burned through over 1.9 million hectares between January and the end of September this year, a monitor analysing satellite imagery said on Monday.

data.title: North Korea warns 'grave situation' prevailing along border
data.description: SEOUL — The powerful sister of North Korea's leader said Monday that "a grave situation is prevailing" along the Southern border, according to state media, and Pyongyang was considering deploying "more tactical strike means" to the area.

data.title: Australian lawmaker critically hurt in 'deliberate attack'
data.description: SYDNEY - Australian independent lawmaker Helen Haines was struck by a car and suffered "critical injuries" on Monday in what Prime Minister Anthony Albanese described as a deliberate attack.

data.title: Credit card fraud reports over iPhone Duo pre-orders jump to 130 cases in Hong Kong
data.description: Hong Kong police have received nearly 20 more reports of unauthorised credit card transactions for iPhone Duo pre-orders over the weekend, bringing the total amount involved to HK$5 million (21 million baht).
